key_insight: PG-KINN combines a KAN trial network with a Petrov-Galerkin weak formulation to improve PDE solving by reducing derivative order, improving conditioning, and supporting forward and inverse problems.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate and robust physics-informed surrogate for computational mechanics, especially for nonlinear, non-self-adjoint, and complex-geometry PDEs.
method: KAN as the trial space with learnable spline activations
Independent compactly supported piecewise-polynomial test functions
Gauss-Legendre quadrature after integration by parts to form element-wise weak residuals
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over MLP baselines and prior KAN variants across benchmarks including crack singularities, stress concentration, hyperelasticity, inverse identification, and complex geometries.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful Petrov-Galerkin test-space design and quadrature setup, and the method may be more implementation-intensive than standard strong-form PINN training.
paper_title: PG-KINN: A Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs
